entities.name: Jean Crespin
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jean Crespin was a French Protestant lawyer who became a significant printer and martyrologist in Geneva.

Born in the early 16th century, Crespin rose to prominence as a key figure in the Protestant Reformation, using his printing skills to disseminate anti-Catholic pamphlets and promote the teachings of John Calvin.

Crespin's most notable contribution was the publication of the Martyrologium Genevensis, a comprehensive collection of biographies of Protestant martyrs who were executed in Geneva during the reign of the Catholic Duke of Savoy.

Through his work, Crespin played a significant role in shaping the Protestant identity of Geneva and contributing to the development of the city's Protestant community.

Despite his influence, Crespin's legacy was largely overshadowed by that of other Protestant leaders, such as John Calvin and Huldrych Zwingli, and he remains a relatively minor figure in the history of the Reformation.

In 1572, Crespin died under mysterious circumstances, leaving behind a legacy as a pioneering printer and martyrologist who played a significant role in shaping the Protestant identity of Geneva.
